from.place: the local finite-projective calculation underlying the comparison isomorphism

title: Internal Hom from a strictly perfect complex
statement: Let U be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let P be a strictly perfect bounded complex of finite projective O_U-modules [def-pc-perfect-complex]. For every complex M of O_U-modules, the derived internal Hom R\mathcal Hom_{O_U}(P,M) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is represented by the ordinary Hom complex \mathcal Hom^\bullet_{O_U}(P,M), and the canonical comparison from the ordinary Hom complex to derived internal Hom is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Represent M by a cochain complex and choose the functorial K-injective resolution M^bullet \to I^bullet supplied in the definition of derived internal Hom. By that definition, R\mathcal Hom_{O_U}(P,M) is represented by the Hom complex Hom^bullet(P,I^bullet).

Let f:M^bullet \to I^bullet be the resolution of Step 1; we show Hom^bullet(P,M^bullet) \to Hom^bullet(P,I^bullet) is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. For each degree i, P^i is a direct summand of a finite free module [def-pc-perfect-complex], so \mathcal Hom(P^i,-) is exact: it is a direct summand of the exact functor \mathcal Hom(O_U^{\oplus r},-) of [lem-sc-finite-free-internal-hom-exact]. An exact functor commutes with taking cohomology sheaves, so \mathcal Hom(P^i,M^\bullet) \to \mathcal Hom(P^i,I^\bullet) is a quasi-isomorphism. P is bounded, so its stupid truncations \sigma_{\geq k}P give a finite filtration of P by subcomplexes with graded pieces P^k[-k]; since the terms of the Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex] are finite products over the degrees of P, applying Hom^bullet(-,M^\bullet) and Hom^bullet(-,I^\bullet) gives termwise split short exact sequences of complexes, compatible with f, 0 \to Hom^bullet(P^k[-k],-) \to Hom^bullet(\sigma_{\geq k}P,-) \to Hom^bullet(\sigma_{\geq k+1}P,-) \to 0, whose first term is a shift of \mathcal Hom(P^k,-) applied to the complex. Induction on the finitely many nonzero degrees of P, using the long exact cohomology sequence of a short exact sequence of complexes (Stacks Tag 0117) and the five lemma, shows that Hom^bullet(P,M^bullet) \to Hom^bullet(P,I^bullet) is a quasi-isomorphism.

The quasi-isomorphism in Step 2 identifies the ordinary Hom complex Hom^bullet(P,M^bullet) with the derived representative Hom^bullet(P,I^bullet), hence gives the comparison isomorphism in D(O_U). The comparison is canonical, natural in P and M, and independent of the chosen representatives because the derived internal-Hom construction is functorial on pairs of complexes and sends quasi-isomorphisms in either variable to quasi-isomorphisms, as stated in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].
